# GEO report: atlas-roadmaps **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 13.08 ÷ 23 × 100 = 57. High = (13.08 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 57. Both are capped at 40 because of a blocker (see below). Your own config says AI search tools should be able to find the site, but `robots.txt` blocks Bing's crawler from the whole site. That is a blocker on GEO-009, which caps the score at 40. Without the cap the raw number would be 57. Nothing is left unknown. Everything below is read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking Bingbot - **Why it matters:** `geo.config.json` says AI search crawlers are allowed, but Bing's crawler is told to stay out of every page. Bing's index feeds several other search products. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:5-6` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: Bingbot` / `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small. Delete those two lines and the blank line after them. Keep the `GPTBot` block, because blocking training crawlers is your declared choice. - **Score after this:** 83. This clears GEO-009 and GEO-014 and removes the cap. ### 2. Add a `Sitemap:` line to robots.txt - **Why it matters:** The sitemap file is valid, but `robots.txt` doesn't point crawlers to it. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: *`. No line in the file starts with `Sitemap:`. - **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://atlasroadmaps.example/sitemap.xml`. - **Score after this:** 92, counting item 1 too. ### 3. Put the changelog text in the server HTML - **Why it matters:** Entries load in the browser after the page arrives, so a crawler that doesn't run scripts sees an empty list. The `/api/changelog` route this fetches from also isn't in the repo. - **Where:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5` - **What the code says:** `useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/changelog').then((r) => r.json()).then(setEntries); }, []);` - **Size:** Medium. Use a Remix `loader` and `useLoaderData`. - **Score after this:** 95, counting items 1 and 2 too. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and a sane size | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, plain text with valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers get the access you declared | Problem | `public/robots.txt:5-6`. Blocker, cap 40. `GPTBot` block is a training choice and isn't counted | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | 0 of 4 routes clear: `public/robots.txt:5-6` blocks Bingbot from all of them. No `noindex` on public pages. `/dashboard` is deliberately noindex, disallowed and not in the sitemap | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical per page | Problem | `/pricing` has none (`app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`, no `meta` export). `/`, `/features` and `/changelog` are fine: 3 clear, 1 problem | | GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5`. `/`, `/features` and `/pricing` are server-rendered: 3 clear, 1 problem | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD (structured data) is valid | Not applicable | None found in any file | | GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, but `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Clear | `app/root.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. `/pricing` inherits the root title and description from `app/root.tsx:2` | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable through real links | Problem | `/features` is reached only by `
navigate('/features')}>` (`app/routes/_index.tsx:9`). `/pricing` and `/changelog` are in the nav: 2 clear, 1 problem | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions blocking AI search | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` in the `meta` exports, and no header config in the repo | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Read all 6 files. No images or icon-only controls, and every page has a title | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app profile | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | None present | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not scored | None present | ## Other problems found - **`/features` is missing from the main navigation, and the home page reaches it with a click handler:** `app/root.tsx:7` has `
Pricing Changelog
` and `app/routes/_index.tsx:9` has `
navigate('/features')}>`. Add `Features` to the nav, or change the div to a `Link`. - **`/pricing` has no canonical, and gets only the generic root title "Atlas":** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`. Add a `meta` export with its own title, description and canonical. ## Worth considering - **Back up the integrations claim:** `app/routes/_index.tsx:8`: `Integrates with all the tools you already use.` Nothing names a single tool. A list of the real integrations gives readers and machines something concrete to quote. - **Say what plans cost:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`: `Plans that grow with your team. Talk to us for a quote.` The page names no plans or prices. Plan names, what each includes, and prices if you can share them would answer the first thing a visitor comes to ask. - **Flesh out the Features page:** `app/routes/features.tsx:1`: `Timelines, sharing and status updates.` It promises three features and describes none. A short section per feature would help. - **Give the changelog dated entries:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:6` renders bare `
  • ` strings. Dates and version headings, and perhaps a page per release, would give each release its own address. - **Add `` dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-6` lists four URLs with no dates. The changelog at least has real dates. - **Label the site with Organization/WebSite structured data:** nothing in the repo states the site's name or links in machine-readable form. `geo.config.json` already gives the origin `https://atlasroadmaps.example`. - **Add basic head tags:** `app/root.tsx:6`: ``. The root `meta` sets no `charset` or `viewport`. - **Give `/pricing` a real title and description:** `app/root.tsx:2` supplies `Atlas` and `Roadmaps your whole team can follow.` for any route without its own metadata. - **Add social tags:** none of the `meta` exports set `og:title`, `og:description` or `og:image`. They control how links to the pages look when shared. - **Add navigation from Features to Pricing:** `app/routes/features.tsx:1` and `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` have no links onward to related pages. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Status codes and headers:** whether the server answers 200 for each URL, and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers set outside the repo, need a live check. - **`/api/changelog`:** no route for it exists in this repo. Confirm where it is served. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools to find this site, matching `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`. Blocking training crawlers (`GPTBot`) is treated as deliberate. - GEO-014 counts the Bingbot block in `robots.txt` against indexability, as the rule's check directs. If you treat it as only a GEO-009 issue, the uncapped number would be 70 instead of 57. After item 1 the score is 83 either way. - Remix v2 behaviour: a route with no `meta` export uses the root's `meta`. - I read all 6 files in `app/`, `public/robots.txt`, `public/sitemap.xml`, `geo.config.json` and `package.json`. That covers all 5 routes, the nav, the shared layout and the only sitemap and robots sources. There is no JSON-LD anywhere. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
